note: Rewritten from the species-level description of Chhotani (1997), originally in English; alates recorded as unknown in the original, with only soldiers and workers described; synonymy, literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records not translated; all measurements are given in mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to brown, labrum slightly paler than head capsule, antennae and legs pale yellow to yellowish brown, mandibles dark brown and paler at base, body milky white to yellow. Cephalic setae sparse, body setae moderate. Body length 4.9–7.4 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, sides slightly convex and slightly narrowed anteriorly (head length to mandibular base 1.75–2.30, maximum width 1.35–1.85, width at mandibular base 0.95–1.18 mm); width 2/3 to slightly more than 3/4 of head length, mandibular base width about 2/3 to 3/4 of maximum width (maximum width/length index 0.68–0.80, mandibular base width/maximum width index 0.63–0.74). Antennae 16–17-segmented, mostly 17; with 16 segments segment 2 longer than segment 3 and segment 4 shortest, with 17 segments segment 2 about twice segment 3 and segment 3 shortest. Postclypeus short, subrectangular, not distinctly delimited from the frons. Labrum ligulate, apex triangular and pointed. Mandibles falcate, stout, 1.10–1.30 mm long, slightly more than half the head length (left mandible length/head length index 0.54–0.63). Left mandible with a prominent tooth at midlength (tooth/mandible length index 0.41–0.50, 0.41 in the type specimen), right mandible with a corresponding small tooth at midlength. Postmentum subrectangular, widest in the anterior third (length 1.15–1.60 mm). Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.60–0.83, width 0.95–1.40 mm), anterior margin rounded with a weak median concavity, posterior margin slightly convex and shallowly concave medially; mesonotum narrower than pronotum, posterior margin distinctly incised; metanotum as wide as or slightly wider than pronotum, posterior margin slightly convex.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Workers dimorphic. Major worker: head capsule pale yellow to yellowish brown, antennae and legs yellow, postclypeus concolorous with head capsule, body white to yellow; cephalic and body setae moderate. Body length 4.0–5.5 mm. Head capsule subcircular, wider than long (head length to mandibular base 1.2–1.65, maximum width 1.35–1.78 mm); fontanelle plate a small white translucent circular spot at the centre of the head. Antennae 17–19-segmented (19-segmented in the type specimen); with 17 segments segment 3 shortest, with 18 segments segment 4 shortest, with 19 segments segment 3 shortest or nearly as long as segments 4 and 5. Postclypeus weakly inflated, less than half as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.40–0.58, width 0.75–1.03 mm), anterior margin rounded with a median concavity, posterior margin convex and concave medially; mesonotum narrower, metanotum slightly wider than pronotum, posterior margin nearly straight. Minor worker: similar to the major worker but smaller, antennae 15–16-segmented; body length 3.0–4.0 mm, head length to mandibular base 0.80–0.88, maximum head width 0.93–1.00, pronotum length 0.30–0.35, width 0.60–0.68 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Thakur (1981) regarded this species and O. meturensis as conspecific and the latter as a synonym, but retained the species provisionally because he had not examined the type specimens of this species. Chhotani examined a paratype soldier of this species deposited in the AMNH and concluded that the two are not conspecific; from the type material of O. ceylonicus, including the lectotype designated by Thakur, he confirmed that O. meturensis is a synonym of O. ceylonicus.
